intent: Slightly advanced sensor y-positions forward by +0.005 from last iteration to further improve early line detection and control anticipation, building on previous forward shift of +0.01. Retain increased sensor size 0.016 and wheel track 0.16 to maintain noise robustness and turning stability. Expect this fine forward adjustment to reduce line loss events and steering oscillations further, improving progress and completion on both oval and s-bend tracks, supporting better generalization.
learning: Request telemetry on completion, progress, rms_error, line_loss_events, and steering_oscillation to verify if the smaller forward sensor shift improves line anticipation and control smoothness. Also monitor if line loss events decrease and progress increases, confirming improved robustness and stability. These measurements will guide whether further fine-tuning of sensor y-positions or other geometry changes are needed.
rationale: Integrator feedback and telemetry show line loss and steering oscillations remain despite previous geometry changes. The last iteration moved sensors forward by +0.01 in y and increased sensor size and wheel track, which improved but did not eliminate issues. A smaller forward shift of +0.005 in sensor y-positions is a fine-tuning step to optimize line anticipation without destabilizing sensor weighting. This should help detect the line slightly earlier, allowing smoother control and fewer line loss events. Maintaining sensor size and wheel track preserves noise robustness and stability gains. This incremental change is expected to improve control smoothness and completion rates, as measured by reduced line loss events, lower rms error, and steering oscillation.
